parts.text: He asked his horse what three plus two was.
The horse tapped his hoof five times.
You see, in Berlin, over a hundred years ago, a maths teacher swore his horse could count.
His name was Hans. He could add. Subtract. Even tell the date.
Crowds packed the yard to watch, and he never charged a penny.
Even The New York Times wrote about him.
So they sent thirteen experts to catch the trick.
They watched the teacher's hands. Nothing.
They asked the questions themselves. Hans still got them right.
Their verdict: no trick at all.
Then a young student named Oskar tried one more thing.
He hid the person asking, where Hans couldn't see them.
Suddenly, the genius horse got almost everything wrong.
Because as the taps reached the right number, people's faces relaxed, without them knowing.
Hans wasn't reading numbers. He was reading faces.
